newsitem.title: USA: Russian space station generator fails, NASA.
newsitem.headline: Russian space station generator fails, NASA.

text.p: A generator that provides oxygen on Russia's Mir space station failed on Friday, forcing the two Russians and one American on board to use a backup chemical system similar to one that sparked a fire two weeks ago, NASA officials said.
The Elektron device, which uses electricity to generate breathing oxygen from waste water, had been experiencing problems all week before finally failing, spokesman Rob Navias said.
Navias said an older, seldom-used back-up system was activated, but was shut down when it also malfunctioned.

Russian flight controllers in Moscow reluctantly instructed the crew to start using chemicals that generate oxygen when heated. The chemical method is usually used to supplement the Elektron device when there are more than three crew aboard.
Aboard the station are mission commander Vasily Tsibliev, flight engineer Alexander Lazutkin and U.S. astronaut Jerry Linenger.

A fire that filled the 11-year-old space station with choking smoke on Feb. 22 was blamed on a crack in one of the so-called chemical candles. One of two devices aboard the station used to heat the candles was destroyed in the blaze.
